% An inline list in a node of text width, framed by a fit node: enumitem
% boxes each item and unboxes it, so the paragraph breaks as TeX breaks it,
% the node's anchors stay known, and no path parts on the fit.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[inline]{enumitem}
\usepackage{tikz}
\usetikzlibrary{positioning,fit,backgrounds}
\newlist{steps}{enumerate*}{1}
\setlist[steps]{label=\color{darkgray!7!black}\emph{\roman*)},itemjoin={{, }},itemjoin*={{, and }}}
\NewDocumentEnvironment{question}{+m +m +b}{\bigskip\begin{tikzpicture}[remember picture,node distance=\baselineskip-5pt]
  \node[inner sep=0pt,text width=\textwidth,align=justify] (B) {#3};
  \node[inner sep=0pt,above=of B.north west,anchor=south west] (Q) {\emph{#1}};
  \node[inner sep=0pt,above=of B.north east,anchor=south east] (R) {#2};
  \tikzset{remember picture,overlay}
  \node[rounded corners=1mm,inner sep=3mm,fill=lightgray!20,fit=(Q)(R)(B),on background layer] (F) {};
\end{tikzpicture}}{}
\begin{document}
\begin{question}{How is this done?}{Q1}
  A few words before
  \begin{steps}
    \item the first step of the work
    \item the second step with more words
  \end{steps}.
  Some words follow the list here.
\end{question}
\gdef\SatexReachedEnd{}
\end{document}
